Definition: feminine of G2190; hostility; by implication, a reason for opposition:--enmity, hatred.
BiblicalUsage: Enmity is settled hostility, not a passing quarrel, and the New Testament uses it for the deepest divides. Paul says the carnal mind is enmity against God, lists hatreds among the works of the flesh, and says Christ broke down the wall of enmity between Jew and Gentile in His own body. James warns that friendship with the world is enmity with God, so the word always forces a choice of sides.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe Christ is the only one who can end real enmity, because He did it by taking the hostility into Himself on the cross. My position is that peace with God is not a truce; it is the end of the war.
